text:
Asha Patel: Quick design callout 0m ago 00000000000Sharing a prototype for the settings form. Need alignment on validation affordances and how we surface destructive actions. Thoughts?
Samir Liu: For validation: field-level inline errors for syntactic issues (email format, length) and an unobtrusive top banner for server-side submit errors (rate limit, quota). Inline errors should be announced immediately by screen readers.
Eli Gomez: Yes. Also keep inline text lightweight (one line). Avoid big colored blocks under every field or it'll feel noisy. For server banner, include a concise action link: "Retry" or "Contact support".
Maya Chen: Placement question: the "Delete workspace" action currently sits as a red button in the page header. Users hit it by mistake during keyboard nav. Should we move it to the bottom with the rest of destructive settings?
Asha Patel: I'm torn. Header is discoverable for power users. Bottom is safer. Maybe keep it in header but reduce prominence (outline style), and require an additional confirm step.
Samir Liu: Accessibility requirements: any confirm flow must trap focus, label purpose clearly, and not rely on color. For typed-confirm, provide clear instructions and require exact match. That prevents accidental deletes.
Eli Gomez: Another idea: Progressive inline confirm that expands under the button instead of a modal. Inline confirm keeps context and is faster for keyboard users. But we must ensure it works in small viewports.
Maya Chen: Inline confirm is nice UX-wise. We should add an `aria-live` region announcing the expanded confirm so screen readers know it opened. Also include `aria-describedby` on the confirm input explaining permanence.
Asha Patel: Proposed copy for inline confirm: "To permanently delete this workspace, type its name: <workspace-name>". Button text: "Delete workspace permanently". Secondary: "Cancel". Any objections to this tone?
Samir Liu: Copy is clear. Slight tweak: avoid the word "permanently" repeated; use it once. Eg. label: "Type the workspace name to confirm deletion" then button "Delete" with visually red style and `aria-label` "Delete workspace permanently".
Eli Gomez: Technical note: when showing inline errors, set `aria-invalid=true` on the input and toggle an `id` for the error `div` referenced by `aria-describedby`. Use `role=alert` on the error node to prompt SRs to read.
Maya Chen: For required-field signposting: asterisk only vs "Required" hint. Asterisk is compact but not everyone understands it. I suggest a small legend at the top: "* Required" plus screen-reader-only text on each label that says "required".
Asha Patel: Agreed on legend + sr-only. That keeps visuals clean and meets discoverability.
Samir Liu: On animations: don't push layout when errors appear. Use fade + scale to avoid page jump and to preserve focus position. Also add e2e tests verifying SR announcement behavior.
Eli Gomez: One more edge: server-side validation that maps to field errors (e.g., name reserved) should surface as inline on the field rather than a generic banner so the user knows where to fix it. Banner reserved for global failures (auth, quota, server down).
Maya Chen: About small screens: modals are sometimes necessary because inline confirm may be off-screen. If using inline confirm, fallback to modal for viewports < 420px. Keep copy identical.
DesignBot: Auto-scan results: missing `aria-invalid` on sample inputs, recommended `aria-live` region id for confirm reveal, check color contrast for default error text (contrast ratio 3:1, recommend 4.5:1).
Asha Patel: Great callouts. I'll iterate the prototype: inline field errors (announceable), top dismissible banner for server errors, asterisk + form legend for required, inline typed-confirm for delete with modal fallback on small screens, and animation to avoid layout shift. Posting updated frames in ~45m. :sparkles:
Samir Liu: SGTM. Please include the markup snippets so eng can implement.
Eli Gomez: I'll add SR-focused tests to the e2e backlog.
Maya Chen: Thanks all 0000000:heart:
